title: Repair the wrong-segment event id in the four mounted events siblings
goal: Make every app/api/admin/events/[id]/* sibling resolve the event UUID from the [id] segment and verify the resource at the data boundary.

in: The four mounted sibling routes of task-messages
out: The registry proof harness (ADMIN-016 already corrected task-messages)

resume_condition: The task is selected as the owner's next collision-free work item.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-1: no route under app/api/admin/events/[id] reads a path segment other than the [id] segment, proven by a test that mounts a real UUID and asserts the event_task_messages / event_group_chats / event_secure_uploads predicate value.
evidence: All 9 wrong-segment reads repaired: communications/route.ts:23,107,215; communication-settings/route.ts:38,78; group-chats/route.ts:27,103; secure-uploads/route.ts:26,113,243 now call resolveEventIdFromRequest (segment after the literal "events" segment, URL-decoded, UUID-validated, 400 "Invalid event id" otherwise) — the ADMIN-014 / events-[id]-analytics shape, not a new scheme.

__tests__/admin/event-communications-resource-scope.test.ts:5 tests assert the actual predicate value reaching event_bulletins, event_group_chats, event_group_messages, event_secure_uploads, event_task_messages and events_v2 with a real UUID mounted in the path, and that the literal route name never appears.

The same file walks all 23 route.ts files under app/api/admin/events/[id] and asserts none indexes a fixed path segment and that every path split resolves through indexOf("events") or extractIdFromPath. Verified: no other route in the family had the defect.

__tests__/admin/admin019-base-sha-proof.test.ts:4 tests regenerate the four route files from git show 16fb834f into a mirror under __tests__/admin/.admin019-base-mirror (removed in afterAll), dynamically import them and assert the base behaviour. The shared worktree is never reverted.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-2: lib/admin/api-route-registry.ts records the enforced class for each repaired method, and __tests__/admin/admin-registry-guard-proof.test.ts stays green.
evidence: npx vitest run __tests__/admin/admin-registry-guard-proof.test.ts -> 10 passed, green after the repair.

AC-2 is met without a registry edit: ADMIN-016 had already reconciled all four routes. enforced class per method is recorded for /api/admin/events/[id]/communications and /communication-settings at route level (capability_gated, capability event.view, capabilityByMethod PATCH+POST and PATCH respectively, GET inheriting the route capability) and explicitly per method for /group-chats (authClassByMethod GET+POST authenticated_user) and /secure-uploads (authClassByMethod DELETE+GET+POST authenticated_user).

The repair preserved withAdminCapability("event.view") on communications and communication-settings and withAuth on group-chats and secure-uploads, so every declared authClass, capability literal and resourceBoundary marker still matches the source; the proof test compares all three against the route source and reports zero errors.

lib/admin/api-route-registry.ts is owned by ADMIN-020/021/022/023 and was NOT edited by ADMIN-019. The exact per-method record ADMIN-019 measured is recorded in this task under registry_entries for them to reconcile; no registry change was required for the proof test to stay green.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-3: cross-tenant denial is proven - a user who is not an event participant, event owner, or admin/manager event participant gets 403 on every method of all four routes.
evidence: event-communications-resource-scope.test.ts "denies a user with no event relationship on every method of all four routes": 14 denial requests covering GET/POST/PATCH of communications, GET/PATCH of communication-settings, GET (list + messages) and POST (message + create) of group-chats, and GET (list + download), POST and DELETE of secure-uploads all return 403 for a user with no participant row, no ownership and no employment assignment.

Anti-vacuity control in the same test: the identical 13 requests are then replayed as the owner of the same event and every one returns 200, so the 403s cannot come from a route that is simply broken.
A second anti-vacuity control replays the event-B denials for the event-A owner and then authorises the same request shapes on event A.

Base-SHA proof of vacuity: at 16fb834f all four routes return 403 to the OWNER of the mounted event (admin019-base-sha-proof.test.ts, ownerStatuses [403,403,403,403]), so a bare 403 assertion would have passed at base for the wrong reason.

npm run check:admin-route-registry -> 291 route files, 53/53 legacy, REL-103 check OK
npm run agents:validate -- --strict -> 18 agents, 225 tasks, 103 pending handoffs, 0 warnings, 0 errors

progress.summary: AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3 met. All nine wrong-segment reads in the four mounted events siblings now resolve the event UUID from the [id] segment through resolveEventIdFromRequest (the ADMIN-014 / analytics shape: segment after the literal 'events' segment, URL-decoded, UUID-validated, 400 otherwise). Two mutation branches with no authorization at all were found and closed, as ADMIN-014 found in its sibling: communications PATCH mark_read/acknowledge ran no gate and wrote with no event predicate, and group-chats POST create-group ran no gate and could create a group plus upsert arbitrary participants in any event. Three data-boundary gaps also closed: group-chats GET ?messages had no event predicate on event_group_messages, secure-uploads POST completed a task message from any event via task_message_id, and secure-uploads DELETE wrote with no event predicate. 17 new tests; the base-SHA mirror proves the 403s are non-vacuous.

registry_entries.registry_baseline: npm run check:admin-route-registry after the repair: 291 route files, 53/53 legacy, REL-103 OK. No route was added, removed, or reclassified, so the exact legacy baseline is unaffected.

communications.extra: PATCH mark_read and PATCH acknowledge ran NO membership gate at all and their UPDATE carried only .eq("id", id) with no event predicate; PATCH now resolves the same participant OR event-owner OR worker-assignment union as GET and every bulletin UPDATE/DELETE carries .eq("event_id", eventId).

communication-settings.predicate_after: the real [id] UUID on both the ownership read and the settings UPDATE
communication-settings.extra: No missing gate found: GET required participant OR owner, PATCH required owner, and the settings UPDATE was already .eq("id", eventId).

group-chats.extra: POST create-group ran NO authorization at all: any authenticated user could create a group in any event AND upsert arbitrary user ids as event_participants of that event. Now gated on participant OR event owner before any write. GET ?messages=true&groupId= had no event predicate on event_group_messages and no group membership check; it now resolves the group with .eq("id", groupId).eq("event_id", eventId) (404 otherwise), requires group membership (403 otherwise), and predicates the message read on event_id.

secure-uploads.extra: No missing gate: GET/POST require isOwner OR participant, DELETE requires event owner. Two data-boundary gaps closed: the task_message_id completion side effect read and updated event_task_messages with .eq("id", taskMessageId) only, so a participant could complete a task in ANY event by attaching its id; both now carry .eq("event_id", eventId) and the read is maybeSingle(). The final DELETE also carried only .eq("id", uploadId) and now carries .eq("event_id", eventId).

base_sha_proof.method: The four base route sources are read with git show 16fb834f:<path>, written to a generated mirror at __tests__/admin/.admin019-base-mirror, dynamically imported, exercised with the same fake Supabase client, and deleted in afterAll. The shared dirty worktree is never stashed, reverted, or checked out.
base_result: Every route predicate is the literal route name, never the mounted UUID: communications -> "communications", communication-settings -> "communication-settings", group-chats -> "group-chats", secure-uploads -> "secure-uploads". All AC-1 assertions fail at base.
Every owner GET returns 403 at base ([403, 403, 403, 403]): the feature was dead for everyone, so a bare 403 denial test passes vacuously at base.
Owner mutations are denied at base: communications POST 403, PATCH 404, communication-settings PATCH 403, secure-uploads POST 403, DELETE 403.

Two mutation branches with no authorization at all are reachable by an unrelated authenticated user at base: group-chats POST create-group returns 200 and inserts a group with event_id "group-chats" created_by the stranger, and communications PATCH mark_read returns 200 and writes the stranger into read_by.

residual_findings: group-chats POST create-group still upserts any requested member_id that is not already an event participant into event_participants. That is now reachable only by a member of that same event, so it is no longer a cross-tenant write, but it is still an in-tenant participant-roster write by any participant (including a plain staff role). ADMIN-019 did not change it because it is a product behaviour (invite-by-adding) rather than the segment defect; it needs its own bounded decision.

secure-uploads POST marks a task message complete as a side effect for any event member, not only its sender/recipients. It is now event-scoped at the data boundary, so it is in-tenant, but the narrower ADMIN-014 rule (sender OR recipient OR owner OR admin/manager participant) is not applied on this path.

The communications family is still capability_gated on event.view for all three methods while its resource boundary is event membership; the accepted participant-access risk recorded on 2026-09-13 still applies, and a PATCH participant action is now reachable for a participant who holds the capability.
